column3: Heading 3 uses a vague quantifier, non-standard capitalisation and breaks parallelism with headings 1 and 2.
column4: Revision proposed at [15]: '3. A few Thematic highlights' to '3. Thematic highlights'. Three grounds: (i) FAOSTYLE 3.1 lists 'a few' among the quantifiers to avoid as conveying no useful information, and it also understates a section running from [15] to [24]; (ii) 'Thematic' is capitalised mid-heading, against FAO sentence case for headings; (iii) headings 1 and 2 open on the substantive noun, so the quantifier breaks the set. Please confirm.

column3: Section 3 carries two distinct movements under a single heading.
column4: Structural query on the section the heading at [15] opens: [16]-[19] present the thematic findings from the case studies, while [20]-[24] turn to implementation gaps, implications and the way forward. Ten paragraphs under one heading is heavy for a 24-paragraph introduction with only three sections. Options: (a) split at [20] into a new numbered section 4; (b) insert a third-level heading at [20]; (c) leave as is. FAOSTYLE 2.2.3 permits up to four heading levels. Author decision - no editorial change made.

column3: Heading hierarchy is flat; the title is not a heading.
column4: Recorded for completeness alongside rows 1-2: the title at [0] is bold body text rather than a heading, and all four section headings sit at first level, so the document has no top-level title and the sections render level with it. Proposed: [0] to first level, and [1], [10], [15], [25] to second. Structural only - no wording affected. Handled in the accompanying replacement list; no author action needed unless the present levels are intentional.
